title: What the Regulars Order
logline: At a roadside short-eats stall in the city at dusk, a regular orders without looking up, and a friend talks a first-timer into trying the hottest thing on the griddle.
human_question: How much of what we crave is the food, and how much is the ritual of ordering it?

premise.story: An evening at a roadside food stall: the vendor's rhythm, a regular's wordless order, a group of friends pushing a newcomer to try something, and the small satisfactions and disappointments of a single evening's trade.
premise.place: A roadside short-eats or kottu stall on a busy city street at dusk.
premise.experience: Sizzle, smoke and spice; the pull of smell before sight; the small theatre of ordering, waiting and the first bite.

concept_links.why: This is the concept's own story seed: sight, smell, sound and taste making up the everyday sense-sphere world, with wanting arising both spontaneously and through a friend's urging [C004-P:L25] [C004-M:L21].

The vendor's craft and the regular's habitual order sit beside the concept's account of ordinary appetite as one of the many everyday occasions greed-rooted minds arise, without turning either person into a specimen [C005-M:L5].

what_camera_could_observe: Griddle smoke and the vendor's hands
A regular ordering without a word
A newcomer being urged to try something new
The first bite and its reaction
The stall closing up for the night
what_must_be_real: The vendor's actual trade and the customers' own words about why they come. No dialogue written for them.

possible_arc.opening: Smoke and light against a darkening street.
possible_arc.turn: A newcomer tries the stall's specialty for the first time.
possible_arc.ending_open: The stall closes for the night, busy or quiet, as it actually happens.

requirements: An active roadside food stall with a consistent evening trade
A vendor and regulars willing to speak on camera
Safe filming position on a public street

suggestions.name: A roadside short-eats stall in Colombo
suggestions.why: Colombo has many long-running roadside food stalls with steady evening trade.
suggestions.verify: No vendor has been contacted; this is a plausible setting, not a confirmed location.

risks: Turning ordinary appetite into a moral specimen
Food-tourism framing that flattens the vendor's working life
Traffic and safety on a busy street
drop_if: No vendor will allow filming through a full evening's trade

connections.note: Two tables: one of habitual daily appetite, one of festive urging to eat more.
